chapter: Massey Hall, race and the record business
title: Meditations on Integration and the concentration camps story
summary: Eric Dolphy told him of barbed-wire camps for civil-rights marchers; the piece's original title; the Nazis in America.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, you've said that in a number of ways, and maintained that a long time, at a time when you were one of the most militant spokesmen that music had. And --

It's a police country, but there's more police in the ghettos. And they're murderers. I was told by Eric Dolphy, I had no way of knowing, nobody knows it, but when he was living in the South, right around the time when Martin Luther King was reigning, that they built concentration camps, with barbed wire and all that, and they said all they didn't have was the gas chambers. But he read that in Europe, in some European paper.
Who were they keeping in there?

This was after Martin Luther King -- they allowed him to do so much. But when he kept pressing, they started arresting the crowds and masses and put them outdoors, in these concentration type camps. What did you say? That that Charles wrote the piece he gave the title "Meditations" for a Pair of Wire Cutters, after he heard about those barbed wire camps. "Meditations" the one you heard at Monterey. Yeah: I never knew the full title of that.
That was the original title. It was shortened to Meditations. (inaudible)
That's a much more angry title.
That's where the Nazis went, man. The Nazis came to America.
